text:
Bitcoin holds a fragile floor near $62,000 in Wednesday's Asia session as the Crypto Fear & Greed Index prints at 21 — "Extreme Fear" — reflecting the market's continued digestion of FOMC minutes that signalled a divided Fed and a live September hike probability near 70%. Strategy's disclosure of selling 3,588 BTC in late June added unexpected supply-side pressure, reinforcing caution among institutional desks monitoring corporate treasury behaviour as a leading indicator.

The macro landscape remains hostile to risk. Iran's forces targeted infrastructure in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar following US airstrikes, keeping Brent crude elevated and energy-driven CPI risk on the table. The S&P 500 stabilises at 7,494 (+0.16%) as US equities attempt a tentative recovery, while the 10-year Treasury yield anchors at 4.58% and the DXY holds 101.00. A firm dollar and elevated real yields continue to mechanically suppress Bitcoin's USD valuation, with the $60,000 level now the critical institutional support floor to defend.
